title: Canon question: PR-022's validity condition lapsed in letter but not in purpose
description:
FINDING, made during T-399, deliberately not resolved by the coordinator alone.

PR-022 (authority_tier 1, subject reputation-phase-a) carries this validity condition, verbatim:
  'FORCE-IDENTITY-A is open: no cryptographic identity with an external trust root exists in
   this harness'

After W-002 was signed and applied on 2026-08-17 that sentence is FALSE as written. An enrolled
root exists at .harness/trust/root.pub, nine names are bound inside an operator-signed warrant,
and reconcile traces 19 roll rows to it with 0 orphans.

THE NUANCE THAT MUST NOT BE OVERCLAIMED, and the whole reason this is a task and not a patch:
the DEFECT FORCE-IDENTITY-A is NOT closed. D-17 still holds. Every agent runs as the same OS
user on one filesystem, every agent can read .harness/keys/, and a test proves forgery by
stealing an agent key. So the condition's literal words lapsed while the condition's PURPOSE
survives intact.

THE CANON QUESTION, which is what needs deciding: when a tier-1 record's validity condition is
written as a factual claim, and the fact changes but the concern the fact stood for does not,
does the record lapse? IC-01..IC-10 is the interpretation canon; check whether it already
answers this before legislating anything new.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN. Do not use the lapse to weaken PR-022. Its clause 4 ('NO CONSEQUENCE
ATTACHES. NONE') is the strongest restraint in the layer, and a coordinator that wanted to
attach a consequence would have exactly this incentive to read the lapse broadly. PR-060 was
published without relying on the lapse for that reason; its own validity_conditions depend on
COEXISTING with PR-022 clause 4, not on its expiry. An outcome that leaves PR-022 fully in
force and merely restates the condition in terms of the defect rather than the artifact is a
GOOD outcome, not a failure to act.

Depends on nothing. Blocks nothing. Deliberately low priority: the harness is safe either way,
because the restraint currently binds.
acceptance_criteria: IC-01..IC-10 read and quoted: state whether the canon already answers the lapse question, before proposing anything new.

A written disposal that either (a) restates PR-022's condition in terms of defect FORCE-IDENTITY-A rather than the absence of an artifact, via a tier-1 act naming PR-022, or (b) records that the canon requires no act and why.
Either way: PR-022 clause 4 is still in force at the end, and the disposal says so in words.
The disposal states D-17 explicitly: impersonation is open, agents share one OS user, keys are readable.
If a record is published it needs confirmation by a distinct identity per PR-015 before it binds.
